questions.question: When is the overridden method to run chosen?
options: At compile time, from the reference type
At runtime, from the actual object type
By the order methods appear in the file
questions.explanation: This is dynamic method dispatch: the JVM looks at the real object and runs its version.

questions.question: class Pay { String mode() { return "cash"; } } class Upi extends Pay { String mode() { return "upi"; } } ... Pay p = new Upi(); System.out.println(p.mode()); What prints?
questions.explanation: The reference is Pay, but the object is Upi, so the overridden Upi version runs.

questions.question: class A { public void show() { } } class B extends A { protected void show() { } } Why does B fail to compile?
options: It assigns weaker access than the parent method
protected is not allowed on methods
questions.explanation: An override cannot make access narrower. A public method must stay public in the child.

questions.question: Which parent method CAN be overridden in a child class?
questions.explanation: final locks a method, private is invisible to the child and static methods are hidden, not overridden.

questions.question: class P { static String n() { return "P"; } } class C extends P { static String n() { return "C"; } } ... P ref = new C(); System.out.println(ref.n()); What prints?
questions.explanation: Static methods are hidden, not overridden. The call is bound to the reference type P at compile time.

questions.question: A parent method returns Object. Which return type can an overriding child method use?
questions.explanation: Covariant return types let an override return a subtype of the parent's reference return type.

questions.question: class Base { void save() { } } class Doc extends Base { @Override void save(String f) { } } What happens?
options: Compile error: method does not override a supertype method
It overloads save() without any error
questions.explanation: The parameters differ, so it is an overload, and @Override makes the compiler reject it.

questions.question: class A { String tag() { return "A"; } } class B extends A { String tag() { return super.tag() + "B"; } } ... System.out.println(new B().tag()); What prints?
questions.explanation: super.tag() runs the parent version first, returning A, and the child appends B.

questions.question: class Base { void load() { } } class Kid extends Base { void load() throws Exception { } } Why does this fail?
options: The override adds a broader checked exception
Exception must be caught in Base
questions.explanation: An override cannot throw new or broader checked exceptions than the parent method declares.

questions.question: What does the @Override annotation do?
options: Asks the compiler to check that the method really overrides one
Hides the parent method at runtime
questions.explanation: It is a compile-time check. A wrong name or parameter list becomes a compile error.
